$comment: KB-1c. The plain words Titan may say out loud for each thing an app asks the owner to paste,
and the two catalog taglines that cannot be read aloud as written.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The console publishes the words a customer may never hear: key, keys,
token, tokens, secret, secrets, endpoint, endpoints, relay, proxy, webhook. Every credential
label the Marketplace carries is written for the operator and nearly all of them contain one
('GitHub personal access token', 'Linear personal API key'). Nothing sweeps what Titan SAYS, so
a pack that told him to read those labels out would put a banned word in his mouth on every
connection. This is the mapping, one entry per declared credential field.
`replaces` IS THE ANTI-ROT CATCH. It carries the exact catalog label this phrase stands in for,
so scripts/gen-handbook-packs.mjs fails by name the day that string moves, instead of shipping a
phrase for a label nobody uses. A keyed plugin with no entry here is also a loud failure: a new
plugin cannot ship a banned word into an owner's ear by being forgotten.
A phrase is itself swept, against the same published lists, with vendors that are Marketplace
rows exempted. So 'GitHub' is sayable and 'xai' is not, and neither fact is written down twice.

GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.say: the one thing GitHub gives you when you make a connection for me
GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.why: Three consumers, one box. The owner does not need to know it also reaches the command line in the box.

SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN.say: the one thing Slack gives you after you install the little app in your own workspace
SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN.why: It acts as them, which is the fact that matters to them, and 'xoxp' is not a word anybody has to learn.

LINEAR_API_KEY.say: the one thing Linear gives you on your own account security page
LINEAR_API_KEY.why: Shown once and never again, so naming the page is the part that saves a second trip.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.say: the first of three things Google gives you, the name of the connection
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.why: Google is the row that proves one box per app is false. Numbering them is what stops the owner losing their place.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.say: the second of the three, the private half that goes with that name
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.why: The catalog's own label is a banned word twice over. 'The private half' is what it is.

GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN.say: the third of the three, the long one the sign-in page hands back at the end
GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN.why: Named by where it comes from, because the mistake people make is pasting the short-lived one instead.

TINYFISH_API_KEY.say: the one thing TinyFish gives you on your own dashboard
TINYFISH_API_KEY.why: One box reaches both the connector and the command line. The owner pastes once either way.

NOTION_TOKEN.say: the one thing Notion gives you when you create an integration
NOTION_TOKEN.why: Creating the integration is the step people miss, so the phrase names the step and not the thing.

AIRTABLE_API_KEY.say: the one thing Airtable gives you when you create access for me
AIRTABLE_API_KEY.why: Airtable makes them choose which bases it reaches while they create it, which is the useful half.

TODOIST_API_KEY.say: the one thing Todoist gives you under Settings, Integrations, Developer
TODOIST_API_KEY.why: The worked example. The path is three clicks and saying it out loud removes the whole search.

RESEND_API_KEY.say: the one thing Resend gives you for sending, not the full-access kind
RESEND_API_KEY.why: The full-access one can delete their domains. Naming the narrower choice costs four words.

STRIPE_API_KEY.say: the restricted one Stripe gives you, never your main one
STRIPE_API_KEY.why: Stripe's own word is 'restricted', and this is the one row where pasting the wrong one is expensive.

BROWSER_USE_API_KEY.say: the one thing Browser Use gives you under Billing
BROWSER_USE_API_KEY.why: It spends a balance on every run, and it is filed under Billing for exactly that reason.

BUFFER_API_KEY.say: the one thing Buffer gives you under its own Settings
BUFFER_API_KEY.why: Account-wide with no narrowing, so the right warning is about which account, not which permission.

BROWSERBASE_API_KEY.say: the private one from your Browserbase Settings page
BROWSERBASE_API_KEY.why: Read by the product itself and never handed to a bot, which is why it has no box on a connector page.

BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID.say: the project id on that same Browserbase Settings page
BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID.why: Not private at all, and kept beside the other one because either alone opens nothing.

CODERABBIT_API_KEY.say: the Agentic one from your CodeRabbit account, not the user or workspace kind
CODERABBIT_API_KEY.why: The other two kinds are a different product and the command line refuses them outright.

linkedin.replaces: The application, the page and the token clock
linkedin.say: The application, the page, and the sixty-day clock
linkedin.why: The catalog's tagline is written for the operator and names a word a customer may never hear. Sixty days is the fact underneath it.

buffer.replaces: Schedule to eleven networks with one self-serve key
buffer.say: Schedule posts to eleven networks, and you can set it up yourself
buffer.why: Same reason. 'Self-serve' is the point worth keeping: no application, no review.
